round: the reviewer's second round — six findings (one required, two blocking, three minor) and the architect's ruling on the lock the reviewer left to it

proof.criterion: The reviewer's findings 2, 4, 5 and 6 on the gate — a fail-open on a backslash-escaped quote, a traceback the walk can still reach, a session block whose output is reported as a command, and the info string's silent escape hatch.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh against a fixture carrying every reproduction (the real script symlinked into a miniature repository), and its 168-case suite.
proof.command: a fixture whose scripts/x.sh holds `echo "a \" # b" && bunx biome check .` and `echo don't # bunx biome check .`, whose docs/sealed is a directory at mode 000, and whose docs/solutions/note.md holds a prompted ```console transcript beside a ```sh block ; then PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh over the real tree
proof.observed: The escaped-quote line is reported (`scripts/x.sh:2: this line runs `bunx`, a package runner …`) where it was invisible and the job exited 0; the unclosed-quote twin keeps its comment and passes; the mode-000 directory is `::error file=docs/sealed::docs/sealed cannot be read: [Errno 13] Permission denied`, a named problem with no traceback; and the ```console transcript, whose output line quotes `bunx biome check .`, is unjudged while the ```sh block with the same command is reported at its own line. The tree passes with 13 manifests, 8 workflows, 92 shell scripts and 551 guides, and the suite reports `Results: 168 passed, 0 failed`.
proof.negativeControl: The suite's own `fence-console-info` case still passes, which is why the session fix is the reviewer's alternative rather than its preferred deletion: dropping the five labels, and judging only prompted lines unconditionally, each fail that case, and it is one I may not modify. A session block that carries a prompt is judged at its prompted lines; one that carries none is judged line by line, which is what that case pins. The reviewer's own check that the gate's output over the whole tree is identical with `judged_fence` forced true stands as the evidence that the narrowing hid nothing.

proof.criterion: The architect's ruling on the lock the reviewer raised as its decision — the hold on $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR must be bounded well below the daemon's own installLockWait, and the release path must leave the next role able to install.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of this tree on the issue volume, with a hanging install and a real `flock` contender; and the script's 158-case suite.
proof.command: env … LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=600 LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_HOLD=5 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh against a hanging install, timed ; /usr/bin/flock -w 2 /legion/bun/cache true immediately afterwards ; then the next role's run over the tree it left ; bash scripts/legion-setup.test.sh
proof.observed: The hold ends the attempt, not the budget: exit 0 after 5 s measured against a 600 s budget, reason install-timeout, exitStatus 124, no marker — and `flock` takes the cache immediately afterwards, which is the whole point of the bound. The next role reinstalls over the half-written tree rather than skipping it: the first attempt over it failed once (install-failed, 127 — a lifecycle script resolving modules in a partial tree) and the second succeeded in 8 s and wrote the marker, so recovery converges but can cost one role a failed install. The bound is computed inside the lock beside what is left of the budget and never larger, so a wait and a hold still cannot add past the run.
proof.negativeControl: The number is defended against the derivation rather than today's value: `installLockWait` is `boot × intervals / 3` (120 s at the defaults, 60 s at a halved boot timeout, 1 s at the floor), a role container is told none of those three settings — I checked `roleEnvironment` — so 90 s is an assumption, stated as one, with what it costs where it fails. 90 rather than 60 because four cold installs at this head took 33, 37, 45 and 59 s: a bound inside that spread would cut off every role in turn. `docs/kubernetes.md`'s paragraph that sizes the daemon's wait no longer names only the six roles' plugin installs.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's findings 1 and 3 — a report must not introduce a detail as an install log when no install ran, and a run that never held the lock must not delete a marker it never observed.
proof.surface: packages/pi-legion/src/setup-report.ts's unit tests, a real Oh My Pi pane carrying a lock-timeout report, and the setup script against a holder on the cache's lock.
proof.command: bun test src/setup-report.test.ts ; LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp bun test on a throwaway runLegionPane case ; a holder on the cache with another role's marker in place and LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=2
proof.observed: The notice says `The install log ended: …` only for install-failed, install-timeout and install-killed, and `It reported: …` for lock-timeout and no-install-root, which are the two the script writes from a run that attempted no install; 14 unit tests pass, and on the real binary a pane carrying a lock-timeout report has `It reported:` and no `The install log ended` in its first turn's provider request. A run whose flock expires now leaves the marker exactly as the installing role wrote it, byte for byte.
proof.negativeControl: The same pane with a report whose generation is 9 carries no notice at all (2 pass, 0 fail across the pair), and the install-timeout unit test asserts the `The install log ended:` wording verbatim, so the two branches cannot drift into each other unnoticed.

proof.criterion: AC1 and AC3 — nothing reports a passing lint without the packages, and the install puts the pinned Biome in place without touching the container's disk.
proof.surface: This role container with no node_modules and a poisoned bunx cache, and the throwaway copy on the issue volume.
proof.command: bun run lint packages/pi-legion/ ; bun run typecheck ; then sh scripts/legion-setup.sh cold in the copy, ./node_modules/.bin/biome --version, bun run lint ., cksum bun.lock
proof.observed: Each prescribed command exits 1 with the wrapper's message. The install: exit 0 after `1986 packages installed`, biome `Version: 2.4.11`, `Checked 1079 files`, `cksum bun.lock` unchanged at 581893351 340936, no report, and a second role at 0.037 s with the cache byte-identical.
proof.negativeControl: In the same container `bunx biome check .` exits 0 having checked nothing and `bunx biome --version` answers 0.3.3.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh: the comment scan's backslash handling and its unclosed-quote second pass, `OSError` around the walk's listing and probes, session fences judged at their prompts, and the header's record of the info string as an escape hatch.
scripts/legion-setup.sh and .test.sh: `LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_HOLD` (90 s) bounding the hold inside the lock, the marker no longer deleted by a run that never held it, and cases for both.
packages/pi-legion/src/setup-report.ts and .test.ts: the detail introduced as an install log only where an install ran.
docs/kubernetes.md: the setup section's second bound, and the paragraph that sizes the daemon's installLockWait, which named the wrong set of holders of that inode.
trickyParts: The session-fence fix could not be the deletion the reviewer preferred: the suite's `fence-console-info` case asserts that an unprompted ```console block is judged, and it is a case I may not modify. The shape that satisfies both is prompt-aware — judged at its prompts when it has them, line by line when it does not — and the reply on that thread offers to take the case to the architect if the reviewer still wants the labels gone.

60 s for the hold was inside the measured spread of a cold install (33–59 s across four runs at this head), which would have cut off every role in turn; 90 s is above the spread and still under the daemon's 120 s wait.

A run cut off by the hold leaves a tree whose next `bun install --frozen-lockfile` can itself fail once on a lifecycle script (measured: 127), succeeding on the run after. Recovery converges, and the cost is one role's install — recorded in the body rather than smoothed over.
deviations: The session-fence finding is fixed by the reviewer's named alternative rather than its preferred deletion, for the reason above, and the thread says so plainly.
openQuestions: Unchanged: AC3's full line, AC4's daemon half and AC5's two-role form are production-check criteria, needing the worker image pin and the one `runtime.kubernetes.setup` line — which must name none of the runtime-owned variables.

The `Fast-follow` is unchanged from round 1: the guard's header duplicates its own subcommand table, `legion.ts`'s notice fan-out has no test on the delivered order, and one sentence of `docs/kubernetes.md` still places the lock in `/legion/bun/state`.
discoveredComplexity: The gate's lock and the daemon's plugin install share an inode that neither piece's documentation named. Bounding our hold was the cheap half; the dear half was that the bound has to be defended against a derivation the pod cannot read, so it is an assumption with a knob and a paragraph rather than a computation.

Every defect this round removed was a statement that was true of most lines and false of some: the install-log prefix, the comment scan, the session block. A gate that talks to agents is a thing whose sentences need tests as much as its behaviour does.
